propositions.name: aether_is_medium
propositions.statement: There exists an aether through which solid bodies move and which can alter their dimensions.
propositions.quote: the negative result of which has led FitzGerald and myself to the conclusion that the dimensions of solid bodies are slightly altered by their motion through the aether.

propositions.name: earth_has_translation
propositions.statement: The Earth's annual motion is a translation shared by all systems on it, and it can influence electric and optical phenomena.
propositions.quote: The problem of determining the influence exerted on electric and optical phenomena by a translation, such as all systems have in virtue of the Earth's annual motion

propositions.name: fixed_coordinate_system_exists
propositions.statement: There is a fixed system of coordinates in which the fundamental equations of the theory of electrons hold.
propositions.quote: Then, if we use a fixed system of coordinates,

propositions.name: system_has_definite_velocity
propositions.statement: A system as a whole possesses a definite constant velocity w in a definite direction relative to the fixed coordinate system.
propositions.quote: I shall now suppose that the system as a whole moves in the direction of x with a constant velocity w

propositions.name: additive_velocity_composition
propositions.statement: The velocity of a point of an electron is the sum of the system velocity w and any additional velocity u the point may have.
propositions.quote: any velocity a point of an electron may have in addition to this, so that

propositions.name: true_time_versus_local_time
propositions.statement: There is a true time t of which the local time t' is a derived, distinct quantity that depends on position.
propositions.quote: The variable t' may be called the local time ; indeed, for k=1, l=1 it becomes identical with what I have formerly understood by this name.

propositions.name: simultaneity_across_frames_defined
propositions.statement: A moment in the moving system is put into correspondence with a moment in the resting system by equating true time in one with local time in the other.
propositions.quote: we shall define corresponding instants, the one belonging to P' , the other to P , by stating that the true time at the first instant is equal to the local time

propositions.name: restriction_velocity_below_c
propositions.statement: The velocity of translation must be smaller than the velocity of light for the theory to apply.
propositions.quote: The only restriction as regards the velocity will be that it be smaller than that of light.

propositions.name: fundamental_electron_equations
propositions.statement: The fundamental equations of the theory of electrons are taken as the starting point for describing all electromagnetic phenomena.
propositions.quote: I shall start from the fundamental equations of the theory of electrons.

propositions.name: electrons_are_spheres_at_rest
propositions.statement: Electrons are spheres of radius R when in the state of rest and have their dimensions changed by the effect of a translation.
propositions.quote: the electrons, which I take to be spheres of radius R in the state of rest, have their dimensions changed by the effect of a translation

propositions.name: state_of_rest_is_absolute
propositions.statement: There is a definite state of rest of an electron, relative to which its true spherical shape and radius are defined.
propositions.quote: the electrons, which I take to be spheres of radius R in the state of rest, have their dimensions changed by the effect of a translation

propositions.name: contraction_only_along_motion
propositions.statement: A translation influences the dimensions of separate electrons and of a ponderable body only in the direction of the motion.
propositions.quote: the influence of a translation on the dimensions (of the separate electrons and of a ponderable body as a whole) is confined to those that have the direction of the motion

propositions.name: charge_preserved_under_deformation
propositions.statement: Each element of volume preserves its charge when the electron is deformed by translation.
propositions.quote: each element of volume is understood to preserve its charge.

propositions.name: all_forces_transform_like_electric
propositions.statement: Forces between uncharged particles and between such particles and electrons are altered by translation in the same way as electric forces in an electrostatic system.
propositions.quote: In the second place I shall suppose that the forces between uncharged particles, as well as those between such particles and electrons, are influenced by a translation in quite the same way as the electric forces in an electrostatic system

propositions.name: unique_equilibrium_configuration
propositions.statement: For a solid body under the attractions and repulsions of its particles there is but one configuration of equilibrium.
propositions.quote: if we take for granted that there is but one configuration of equilibrium

propositions.name: no_true_material_mass
propositions.statement: An electron has no mass other than its electromagnetic mass; there is no true or material mass.
propositions.quote: I shall suppose that there is no other, no "true" or "material" mass

propositions.name: longitudinal_transverse_mass
propositions.statement: An electron behaves as if it had a longitudinal mass m1 when accelerated along its motion and a transverse mass m2 when accelerated perpendicularly.
propositions.quote: in phenomena in which there is an acceleration in the direction of motion, the electron behaves as if it had a mass m 1

propositions.name: molecular_masses_transform_electromagnetically
propositions.statement: The masses of all particles are influenced by a translation to the same degree as the electromagnetic masses of the electrons.
propositions.quote: we suppose that the masses of all particles are influenced by a translation to the same degree as the electromagnetic masses of the electrons

propositions.name: molecular_forces_depend_on_position_only
propositions.statement: Molecular forces are determined by the relative positions of particles independently of the velocities of molecular motion.
propositions.quote: the molecular forces may be taken to be determined by the relative positions, independently of the velocities of molecular motion.

propositions.name: electrostatic_system_has_electromagnetic_momentum
propositions.statement: Every electrostatic system moving with a velocity possesses a certain amount of electromagnetic momentum.
propositions.quote: It may be shown that in every electrostatic system, moving with a velocity

propositions.name: unmodified_theory_requires_couple
propositions.statement: The theory of electrons, unless modified, requires the existence of a turning couple on a charged condenser moving through the aether.
propositions.quote: the theory of electrons, unless it be modified by some new hypothesis, would undoubtedly require the existence of such a couple.

propositions.name: condenser_orientation_definite
propositions.statement: The condenser plates have a definite orientation relative to the velocity of translation, so the axis of z can be chosen perpendicular to them.
propositions.quote: if the axis of z is chosen perpendicular to the condenser plates, the velocity w having any direction we like

propositions.name: electromagnetic_momentum_in_direction_of_motion
propositions.statement: The electromagnetic momentum of a moving electrostatic system has a component in the direction of the motion, calculable from the deformed system.
propositions.quote: we can easily calculate the electromagnetic momentum in the moving system, or rather its component in the direction of the motion.

propositions.name: resting_and_moving_indices_distinguished
propositions.statement: The two systems Σ and Σ' are distinguished as one that moves and one that remains at rest, with primed quantities referring to the resting system.
propositions.quote: referring by the index Σ to a moving system and by Σ' to one that remains at rest

propositions.name: no_translation_recovers_true_time
propositions.statement: For a system without translation the primed quantities become identical with the unprimed ones, and k and l become 1.
propositions.quote: For such a system the quantities with accents become identical to the corresponding ones without accents; also k=1 and l=1.

propositions.name: aether_fills_space_between_particles
propositions.statement: The aether occupies the regions between the particles of a body and surrounds ponderable bodies.
propositions.quote: In corresponding points that are situated either in the aether between the particles, or in that surrounding the ponderable bodies

propositions.name: corresponding_positions_between_systems
propositions.statement: For each particle in the resting system at an instant there is a corresponding particle in the moving system at the corresponding instant occupying the corresponding position.
propositions.quote: if a particle in Σ' has a certain position at a definite instant, a particle in Σ occupies at the corresponding instant the corresponding position

propositions.name: quasi_stationary_form_uncertain
propositions.statement: It is hardly probable that the form of the electron will be determined solely by the velocity existing at the moment considered.
propositions.quote: It is even hardly probable that the form of the electron will be determined solely by the velocity existing at the moment considered.

propositions.name: resting_system_formulae_are_recovered
propositions.statement: The formulae for a system without translation are implied by the general formulae of the theory.
propositions.quote: It is to be remarked that the formulae for a system without translation are implied in what precedes.

propositions.name: fundamental_assumptions_yield_independence
propositions.statement: It should be possible from certain fundamental assumptions to show that many electromagnetic actions are entirely independent of the motion of the system.
propositions.quote: It would be more satisfactory, if it were possible to show, by means of certain fundamental assumptions, and without neglecting terms of one order of magnitude or another, that many electromagnetic actions are entirely independent of the motion of the system.
